thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'ded-prod-7' reporting GPU saturation for tenant ACME-CORP. avg GPU util 98% across the pool, multiple worker OOM/GPU_ERRORS. Paging @oncall-sre.

Elliot: acked — I'll take first look. Pulling metrics/logs now.

Elliot: signal: spike starts ~2026-11-02T15:02Z. Sustained 95-100% for ~8m. p99 latency for ACME endpoints jumped 120ms -> ~900ms. Loadbalancer returning 429/503 intermittently.

Elliot: logs show repeated cuda OOM and batcher queue growth. excerpt:
```
worker-37 | ERROR [2026-11-02T15:07:12Z] GPU_ERROR: cuda out of memory while allocating KV cache
batcher   | WARN  queue length=312 target=64
```

Maya: tagging eng-runtime. Is this a job runaway or sudden customer traffic?

Alice (oncall): stepping in for Elliot. Paging dedicated-ops and infra teams.

Steve (dedicated-ops): on it. Quick question: can we evict preemptible workloads on ded-prod-7 to free capacity? What's current slice mix?

Elliot: pool mix: 60% enterprise reserved, 30% standard reserved, 10% preemptible. ACME is in enterprise slice but looks like they're sending large batched regen jobs (long seq + large batch sizes).

Alice (oncall): immediate mitigations we can enact now:
- throttle ACME burst traffic at routing layer
- pause preemptible tasks
- provision emergency burst nodes and migrate ACME to burst slice (costly)
Need ops + product approval for burst.

Steve: I can eject preemptibles immediately. Running preemptible-eject on ded-prod-7.

Steve: ran:
```
opsctl preemptible-eject --pool ded-prod-7 --dry-run=false
```
Result: evicted 12 preemptible tasks, freed ~4 GPUs. Utilization -> ~92%.

Jane (customer-success): ACME infra lead already DM'd support — they're seeing higher latency. I'll prep a short customer note depending on mitigation.

Alice (oncall): we need ~8 extra GPUs to bring usable util <75% and stop the OOMs. Options:
1) emergency burst: spin up 8 GPUs now (fast, expensive).
2) provision a short-lived isolated pool for ACME (safer, ~30-40m).
3) throttle ACME to reduce batch sizes (low cost, may break some job expectations).

Maya (eng-runtime): migration runbook exists (dedicated-migrate-tenant) but provisioning still takes time.

Alice (oncall): who can sign off on emergency spend? Product/finance needed for >$5k. @Rachel?

Rachel (solutions): verbal product approval for a short emergency burst to stabilize a paying customer. Log estimated spend and tag for review.

Steve (dedicated-ops): issuing scale now (playbook):
```
burstctl scale --region us-west-2 --pool-basis ded-prod-7 --add-gpus 8 --tag emergency_acme_20261102
```
Provisioning started, expected ready ~7m. Routing update queued.

deploy-bot: Rolling update applied to routing service (v2.13.4) — 3/3 instances healthy.

incident-bot: ACTION LOGGED: scale request sc-20261102-83 created by Steve. Billing notified.

Elliot: while nodes spin up, I'm applying a soft throttle on ACME's routing to cap large-batch endpoints to 60% of previous throughput.

Elliot: routing patch applied:
```
route update --tenant ACME-CORP --qos max_batch_rate=0.6 --policy emergency-throttle
```

Elliot: queue length is decreasing, OOM errors dropping. Adding temporary serving limits to reject sequences >4096 with 413 to stop runaway long-seq jobs.

Steve: burst nodes are READY — added 8 A100-equivalent GPUs into ded-prod-7-burst. Creating pool mapping.

Steve: migrating ACME to burst slice now (live):
```
routingctl migrate --tenant ACME-CORP --from ded-prod-7 --to ded-prod-7-burst --drain-time=30s
```

Elliot: migration in progress. Draining in-flight requests; watching for errors.

Jane (customer-success): sending customer update: short note to ACME that we're moving them to a temporary dedicated slice to stabilize performance, expect improvements in minutes, will follow up with timeline/postmortem.

Customer message (Jane): "Hi — we observed elevated latency for some requests. We're moving your traffic to a temporary dedicated slice to stabilize performance. Expect improved latency within minutes. We'll follow up with a postmortem. — Redwood Support"

Alice (oncall): migration complete. ACME now serving from ded-prod-7-burst. GPU util on burst nodes ~65%. Latency trending back to baseline.

Elliot: verifying logs — no new OOMs. p99 for ACME ~140ms. 429/503 errors dropped to near zero.

Maya (eng-runtime): next steps: monitor for 60m, gather ACME job patterns causing spike (large batch + long seq). Recommend follow-up with customer to adjust batch-sizing or schedule heavy jobs off-peak.

Steve: tagging scale request for billing review. Also creating a ticket to add guardrails: auto-buffer GPUs or tenant saturation prevention when a single tenant consumes >X% of shared pool.

Alice (oncall): actions captured:
- Incident owner: Alice
- Mitigations: preemptible eject + routing throttle + emergency burst migration
- Timeline: alert 15:02 -> stabilized 15:40
- Customer comms: Jane sent live update
- Postmortem: assigned to Maya & Elliot, due EOD+2
- Billing: Steve to file emergency spend ticket

Elliot: handing off to next oncall. I'll be offline for 20m. @Alice please continue monitoring.

Alice (oncall): acknowledged. Logging oncall handoff. Incident remains open for monitoring until EOD.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: assigned=Alice, status=stabilized, severity=high, incident_id=INC-20261102-7. Postmortem required.

Rachel: recommend offering ACME credits and an architecture session to prevent recurrence.

Steve: filing ticket for tenant isolation guardrails and an automated preemptible eject policy for single-tenant saturation.

Alice (oncall): thanks all — I'll start the incident timeline and postmortem draft now.

Elliot: will append logs and timeline snippets after I return.

incident-bot: Thread closed for active paging. Monitoring alerts will remain for 1h. Please update the incident tracker: https://incidents.internal/INC-20261102-7
